model_variant: free-cash-flow-to-equity (distributable earnings) DCF at cost of equity; net debt = 0 because borrowings are operating funding of the PDL and loan books

inputs.share_count_basis: 68,067k shares on issue = weighted diluted at 30 June 2026 (FY2026 AR line 8180; performance rights <1.2% in prior years). Held flat: no buybacks, no raise, SBC immaterial.
inputs.net_debt_note: Reported borrowings A$470.7m less cash A$61.5m = A$409m (company-defined net debt A$344.1m, FY2026 AR line 9156). NOT deducted: the facilities fund purchased debt ledgers and the consumer loan book (income-generating assets A$1,294.9m) and are operating funding, exactly as deposits are for a bank. Interest expense (A$37.9m FY2026) is charged inside the flows, which are therefore post-interest flows to EQUITY and are discounted at the cost of equity. Deducting the debt as well would charge it twice (SKILL.md: never FCF/WACC on a post-interest flow, never subtract net debt afterwards).
inputs.last_fcf_note: FY2026 FCFE realised = NPAT A$105.5m less equity retained to fund asset-base growth (A$59.2m) = dividends paid A$46.3m (no buybacks, no issuance). Reported FCF of -A$6.6m is a classification artifact: A$305.2m of PDL acquisitions and consumer-loan funding sit inside operating cash flow.
inputs.sbc_source: FY2026 AR cash flow statement 'Share-based payments' (line 7824): -A$1.4m (reversal); FY2019-25 range -0.7 to +4.3m, <1% of revenue. Treated as SBC-zero (section 7e); house = street basis.
inputs.interest_income_note: Bank interest A$1.3m (AR line 7714) left inside PBT: there is no net cash to match it against and it is immaterial.
inputs.wacc_rationale: Discount rate is an AUD COST OF EQUITY, not a WACC: ACGB 10y ~4.3% (Sep-2026) + 5.5% AUD ERP x beta ~1.2 for a leveraged, credit-cycle-geared consumer-finance operator = ~10.9%, rounded to 11.0%. ONE rate across all three scenarios (section 7f: risk is charged in the flows, not stacked in the rate).
inputs.lease_treatment: Treatment B. Lease interest (A$0.9m) is inside PBT; lease principal (~A$7m) is inside the 2.0%-of-revenue maintenance line together with PP&E/software capex; ROU depreciation is inside the D&A add-back (1.7%) which the maintenance line offsets. Lease liabilities (A$20.6m) are excluded from the bridge. Charged once.
inputs.component_mapping: The engine's fields are re-labelled for a financial: 'ebitda_margin_path' = (profit before tax + D&A) / revenue, i.e. AFTER interest expense (FY2026: (150.2+9.9)/586.0 = 27.3%); 'cash_tax_rate_path' = 30% on PBT (FY2026 effective 29.8%); 'capex_pct_path' = 2.0% maintenance (PP&E + lease principal) PLUS growth reinvestment = revenue growth x equity/revenue (913.9/586.0 = 1.56), the equity that must be retained to grow the PDL/loan asset base at constant leverage (sustainable growth = ROE x retention: FY2027 base 12.3% x 49% = 6%). Year FCF therefore equals NPAT + D&A - maintenance - retained equity = distributable earnings to shareholders.
inputs.notes: MODEL: FCFE / distributable-earnings DCF at cost of equity, run through the owner-FCF component engine with net_debt = 0. WHY: Credit Corp is a debt purchaser and sub-prime lender whose 'capex' is PDL purchases (A$305m FY2026) and loan-book funding booked inside operating cash flow; reported FCF is negative in 5 of 8 years without any distress. The routing table's nearest rows are 'non-bank lender / compounder-of-book' (residual income or BVPS x exit P/B). FCFE = NPAT less the equity retained to grow book is the cash-flow form of the same model: PV of distributable earnings at CoE. Cross-check: base value implies ~1.1x FY2026 book and ~9.8x FY2026 NPAT against a business earning ~12% ROE with 6% sustainable growth ((ROE-g)/(k-g) = 1.2x). First valuation of this ticker; no prior model to reconcile against. FY2027 guidance (NPAT A$110-118m, +4-12%) is met by the base year-1 path (A$112.6m) and the bull (A$116.5m); the bear misses it (A$100m).

historical_growth.growth_divergence_warning: EPS 5yr CAGR (3.6%) is 45% below the equity 5yr CAGR (6.5%) and revenue 5yr CAGR (9.35%): book grew faster than earnings because the FY2020 A$150m equity raise and the FY2024 US collections trough held ROE at 8-13% while the asset base compounded. Base-case growth starts at the 6% sustainable rate (ROE x retention) and decelerates.
historical_growth.notes: fcf CAGRs are computed on NPAT (FY2021 88.1 -> FY2026 105.5; FY2023 91.3 -> 105.5) because reported FCF is negative in 5 of 8 years (PDL purchases inside OCF) and realised FCFE (= dividends) is a payout-policy series, not a growth series. Owner-FCF here is FCFE. Pre-tax+D&A margins FY2019-26: 31.7, 14.0 (COVID), 36.5, 37.3, 29.5, 17.3 (US trough), 26.1, 27.3 -- the base path (27.6 -> 28.0) sits below the 7-year mean (~27.7 incl. both troughs, ~31 excl.) because interest costs are structurally higher post-2022.

base.narrative: FY2027 revenue +6% and PBT margin 25.9% deliver NPAT ~A$112.6m, inside the A$110-118m guidance. Growth decays from the 6% sustainable rate to 2.5%; margin edges to 28% as US asset turnover reaches peer parity; reinvestment falls with growth (11.4% -> 5.9% of revenue). Discount 11% CoE, terminal 2.5%.

bull.narrative: FY2027 NPAT ~A$116.5m at the top of guidance; US pricing normalises and purchasing re-accelerates, UK book reaches the A$150-200m medium-term target, margins reach 30% (still below the FY2021-22 36-37% peak). Heavier reinvestment early (14.5% of revenue) is the cost of that growth. Same 11% CoE; terminal 3%.

bear.narrative: FY2027 misses guidance (NPAT ~A$100m) as US purchasing shrinks; FY2028 is a credit-cycle trough of the FY2024 kind (PBT+D&A margin 18%, revenue -3%) with UK start-up losses written off; recovery stalls 3pp below base (25%) because US pricing stays competitive and AU/NZ supply does not rebuild. Same 11% CoE; terminal 2%.

scenario_narratives.base: Credit Corp compounds distributable earnings at roughly its sustainable rate: ~12% ROE with half retained funds ~6% growth of the PDL and loan books at constant leverage, decaying to 2.5%. FY2027 lands in the middle of the A$110-118m guidance as US operational gains (legal channel, asset turnover near PRA/Encore) offset lower US purchasing, AU/NZ lending grows off the record A$510m book, and the UK pilot is roughly break-even by FY2029. Margins recover to 28% but not to the 2021-22 cheap-funding peak.
scenario_narratives.bull: The US pricing cycle turns: purchasing volumes re-accelerate off the A$62m secured pipeline while the collections platform holds peer-level turnover, the UK book scales to the A$150-200m medium-term target with the under-served market's excess demand keeping losses low, and Wizit broadens AU lending. Revenue grows 8% for two years and margins reach 30%. The stock re-rates from ~9x to a mid-teens P/E.
scenario_narratives.bear: The double-edged cycle bites: a consumer downturn lifts charge-off supply but cuts collection rates on ledgers bought at FY2025-26 prices and lifts loan-book losses, repeating the FY2024 trough (NPAT halved). US price competition persists, so discipline means shrinking volumes; the UK entry meets the same responsible-lending regime that forced incumbents out and is wound back with start-up losses. Margins settle 3pp below base and growth is 2%.

probability_weighted.weights_rationale: Bear lifted from the 15% default to 25%: the model is geared to the credit cycle (two NPAT halvings in seven years, FY2020 and FY2024), the largest segment is now the US where pricing is against it, and the UK entry is an unproven pivot into a regime that has ejected incumbents. Bull cut from 35% to 25%: it needs three independent things (US pricing turn, UK execution, AU supply recovery) to go right together. Base 50%.

valuation_philosophy.summary: Value the distributable earnings of a leveraged consumer-finance operator at its cost of equity, with the growth capital it must retain treated as reinvestment, and never deduct the warehouse debt that funds its earning assets. The stock at ~9x FY2026 earnings and ~1.0x book is priced as ex-growth; the base case implies ~1.1x book, i.e. modest undervaluation, with the bull-bear spread driven by the credit cycle and US pricing rather than by the discount rate.
key_risks_to_valuation: Credit-cycle trough: FY2020 and FY2024 each roughly halved NPAT; a repeat inside the forecast window is the bear case, not a tail
US PDL pricing: purchasing discipline caps growth of the now-largest segment; sustained seller's market leaves the US book shrinking
UK sub-prime lending entry under a regulatory regime that forced prior incumbents out; start-up losses and claims risk
PDL carrying values are accounting estimates (useful life, collection curves); re-estimation can hit reported earnings without a cash event
Funding cost: interest expense rose from A$5m (FY2022) to A$38m (FY2026); the model assumes the post-2022 rate regime persists but no further step-up
Reinvestment coefficient (1.56x equity/revenue) assumes constant leverage; a shift to higher gearing would raise FCFE and value, a de-gearing would lower it
